cells.remarks: Records the grant of the village Kōmyana in the Vōda-vishaya with all its income to the Dīkshita Jagadharaśarman, of the village Padhuvādapāku in the Kōntavēṅga-vishaya. The donee belonged to the Bhāradvāja-gōtra and Mādhyandina-śākhā and was a student of the Yajur-vēda. He was well-versed in the Śrauta and Smārta rites and was strong in astronomy (jyōtiḥ-śāstra). The grant was made on the uchchāyana-ēkādaśī day in the bright half of the Kārtika month when Vishnu is believed to wake up from his four-months' sleep.

cells.language: Sanskrit mixed cha-raotara (Nagari, Telugu and Grantha).
cells.remarks: Registers the gift of the village Kalibhitara-khunda [in the Mahendra-bhoga] to certain Ujjayata-bhatta, of the Vatsa-gotra, by the king. The king was Sri-Bhamakhedi of the Kodanave (i.e. Kodana) family, the lord of five vishayas (panchavishayadhipati). The order of gift is addressed to the officials and people of the Pamchapatra-vishaya. The plates are in very bad state and the characters are not clearly legible so that it is almost impossible to read them. Register the gift of the [amvadi in [Sala]-vishaya. The donee's name is not clear. The gift was issued from Kalinganagara.

cells.date: Saka 1002 Durmati, Vaisakha, su. di. tritiya.
cells.remarks: States that, while Liṅgōji-Paṇḍita was governing the Karṇāṭaka kingdom from Peṇugonda-paṭṭaṇa as a subordinate of Akhammā-dēvi, the younger sister of the king, Mallanna-Paṇḍita who was the head of Brāhmaṇas and the chief officer of the king of Bhāganagar, Nāyappa of the Kāmakhāyana-Viśvāmitra-gōtra, Āśvalāyana-sūtra and Rik-śākhā who was the sthala-karṇam of Lēpākshi in the Kōṇḍapi-nāḍu in Paṇugonḍa-rājya gave some land in Lēpākshi to the temple of the Bhāradvāja-gōtra, Āpastamba-sūtra and Yajud-śākhā, who was the arādhyan at Lēpākshi. It registers also the gift of rates on puck-bullocks, shops, looms and morringas to the samo Kumārayya by the ayyāvas of Ayyāvali, etc., the Vaisya of the 18 gōtras of the Penugonda-paṭṭaṇa and of the Yajamānas of the Lēpākshi-sthala etc., assembled in the temple mandapa of that place for daily offerings and lamps to the god Nañjuṇḍēśvara.

cells.date: Saka 1416 Bahudhanya (wrong), Karttika, su. di. Paurṇima, Wednesday.
cells.remarks: States that a certain Pedda Aholalēndri who was a divan under Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Kṛishṇadēvarāya who was ruling at Peṇugonda, gave some land to Aholalam at Peṇu-Lakshmi Nrisimhasvāmin at -omaghaṭṭa in accordance with the direction given to him by the deity at Ahōbalam in a dream. cells.remarks: The record is incomplete, only the first 3 plates of the set remaining. It stops with the partial description of the qualities of king Śrīraṅga, the son of Podda Veṅkaṭapati who was the second son of Śrīraṅga, the son of the great Rāmarāja who was the minister of Sadāśiva. See the genealogical table, Epigraphia Indica Vol. III, page 288. The king is stated to have been crowned by Tātācārya.

cells.remarks: The Saka date falls into the reign of Virupaksha I predecessor of Bukka II. Registers in detail the incomes that the guarding officers (kaval-doregalu) of Madakaira were to get from the several classes of people, residing in the village. Also specifies the incomes that the ayagaras (i.e., the village servants) of certain villages were to get after the king's share was deducted.

cells.remarks: Registers the grant of land at Kavulpatti, hamlet of Palanivadam made by the king for certain services and charities to be conducted at the time of the festivals of the god Bala-Subrahmanya on the Palani-hill on the bank of the Shanmukhanadi in the Vaigavur-nāḍu. The grant was executed in favour of Subrahmanya-Udaiyar, son of Palniyola Mudaliyar, of the Karkatta-gōtra and Pālani-kēhetra. A certain Palni Venkatarayyar was given land and entrusted with the charity. The coin Rājagōpāli is mentioned.

cells.remarks: The pillar is set upside down and the beginning of the inscription is built in. Records that the assembly of Palaiya-Somiyamanādēvi-chaturvēdimangalam, which was a brahmadaya on the southern bank of the Kāvēri, now issued, in place of an old document which was lost, a new sale-deed to a certain Parakēsari-Vilupparayar, the son of Puravar-Ellan, for certain lands which were irrigated by the Kāvēri-kāl, which he had bought and which they had purchased from him. Refers to the 4th year of the reign of king Rājakēsarivarman (who was pleased to mount a wall (madilēṛi-jundaraju)).

cells.remarks: Beginning lost. Begins with the introduction [S]aka[s], etc. Reports that the assembly of the free village (taniyūr) Rājēndra-chaturvēdimangalam, a brahmādāya in Paṇaiyūr-nāḍu, a subdivision of Rājēndra-vaḷa-nāḍu met in the mandapa called Muṇḍadīśoḷan with Aruḷāḷanḍa-Vigraha and the village assembly of Muṇḍa-vōḷār who gave gift of lands. [date-calculation appendix, No. 619: Śaka 1478, 6th year, Naḷa, Varsha-ritu, [Maka] ra 29, śu. di. ēkādaśī, Monday, Pushya. In A.D. 1557 Naḷa, Pushya combined with Monday on only two occasions :- (i) Simha 4, ba. trayōdaśī (August 3) and (2) Kanya 1, ba. dvādaśī (August 31). Makara 29 was Monday, ba. ēkādaśī but the nakshatra was (not Pushya) Jyēshṭha. It corresponded to A.D. 1556 January 25. In A.D. 1557 on Monday, January 25 (= Makara 29) ba. 11 began at ·26 and ended on the following day at ·34. But the nak. was Jyēshṭha and not " Pushya."]
cells.remarks: Relates to the transaction mentioned in No. 617 above. The order for making the grant was issued by prince Abhirāma Parākrama Aḷagiyaśōkhanār.

cells.place: On a slab set up in front of the Vīrabhadrasvāmin temple in the same village (as Śiva temple). †
cells.date: Śaka 1744, Chitrabhānu, Mārgaśira, śu. di. 10, Monday. [date-calculation appendix, No. 693: Saka 1474, Paridhāvi, Pushya, ba. di., 30, Solar eclipse = A.D. 1553, January 14, Saturday. There was a solar eclipse on Saturday.]
cells.remarks: Relates that Basavalingayya, son of Marayya and Bāramma, the shareholder of a moiety in the mānya-lands of the mathas, Peḍḍgōmatha and Doṇipāḍi and other villages, repaired by raising alms the temple of Vīrabhadrasvāmin at Kōvelakuṇṭla which was in ruins. The merchant classes, on being approached, gave for worship and offering 4 chiṭṭedu of rice and one ruvva-weight of lamp-oil. And on Friday fairs, those who sold by scale, set apart 1 gavaḍi (?) and those who sold by measure, one chiṭṭedu, evidently for the same purpose.

cells.remarks: States that the Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Veṅkaṭādrirāja, son of Kṛishṇarāja and grandson of Nandyāla Nāraṇarāja of the Ātrēya-gōtra, the Āpastamba-sūtra and the Yajuś-śākha granted as sarvamānya, lands in the villages of Kōvilakuṇṭla, Chintakunta, Chinakōperla and ..., the vartana (customary tax) on kabbus (sugarcane) and ... the mānakōṭa and kōlayata collected at Kōvilakuṇṭla for offerings, the bodily and festive enjoyments, the Rāma-nija-kūṭa, the palanquin service and other festivals of the god Vithalēśvara at Kōvilakuṇṭla.

cells.date: Saka 1407, Vijaya vasu, [Asvina], bu. di. ** solar eclipse.
cells.remarks: Helps to the manifestation of the god Ramachandradeva before the 'Eleven Rudras' and to his having received worship at the hand of Cholayya. Registers the construction of the gopuras and the front-mandapas, the several repairs and the performance of sacrifices by Rayaparaja, the grandson of that Chola. He also granted to the god Ramachandra the villages, Ramachandrapura, Isvarapura, Rayasagara, Komudavalli, Sivalinga, in Moligai-simai, in Edadnad, in the Kolar-sima and lands near the tanks of Agali, Maduvidu, Havidu, Kantavalu and Kahi.

cells.date: Śaka 1428, Krōdhana, Chaitra, śu. di. 1, Wednesday. [date-calculation appendix, No. 757: Śaka 1426, Krōdhana (= Ś. 1427) Chaitra, śn. di. 1, Wednesday. Śaka 1426 (= A.D. 1504-05) corresponded to Rakshasa (not to Krōdhana) in which Chaitra śu. 1 was Sunday. In Krōdhana (= Śaka 1427) Chaitra śu. 1, was Thursday the tithi ending at 91 but Quaitra śu 1, in Śaka 1428 (i.e.,) Kshaya Samvat was Wednesday (= A.D. 1506, March 27, Wednesday). The inscription refers to Chaitra at the beginning or Chaitra at the end of a year. Śaka 1426 (= Krōdhana = A.D. 1505-06), which would be the same as Chaitra at the beginning of A.D. 1506-07 (= Ś. 1428 = Kshaya Samvat).]
cells.remarks: Mentions a certain Noḷam[ba]-Gāmuṇḍa.

cells.remarks: Mr. Tarani Charan Rath, B.A., District Munsiff, Ongole, translates the record thus:—During the reign of Ananta Hariharabana Jagadeva, the Raja of Athagoda, this temple was constructed and the image of the king is installed on the pedestal by him, who is ever at His feet. cells.place: On the wall of the Durgapanchika cave at Ramathirtham (Vizianagaram zamindari, Vizagapatam district).
cells.remarks: This is a fresh copy of No. 372 of 1905. The inscription is of the much damaged States that the saint Trikahoyogi Siddhantadeva, the presiding teacher (guru) of the Desigana and the spiritual teacher (guru) of Vimaladitya paid respects to Ramalokapja (i.e. Ramathirtham hill), with great devotion. The king is given the titles Rajaraja-Narendra and Sarvaloka-Bhima.

cells.place: On the front of the smaller shrine in the conserved Ramanuja-matha on the hill of Govinda. †
cells.remarks: Much peeled off. At the beginning and end of the top line are seen the expressions Sri-a-and mummuri respectively, engraved in Chalukyan characters. The two letters Sri and Sa, evidently the beginning of some name the rest of which is lost, are engraved here in Chalukyan characters to the size of about a foot in height. The position and condition of the gorge suggest that there might have been some caves here.

cells.remarks: Gives a detailed genealogy of the chiefs of Chenji (i.e. Gingee) and states that Varadappa-nayaka of this family gave some land and a golden palanquin (amḍala) to the god Kumārasvāmin on his way back from Sētu (i.e. Rāmēśvaram) whether he had gone on a pilgrimage. cells.remarks: Gift of free of taxes as a dēvadāna to the temple of Tirumuḍugam-Uḍaiyār of Paravūr-kūṟṟam in Iruṅgōḷap-pāḍi. The lands were variously situated in Edirili-śōḷanallūr, a hamlet of Muḍigoṇḍaśōḷa-chaturvēdimaṅgalam in Māra-nāḍu, a subdivision of Virudarājabhayan-kara-vaḷanāḍu, to the temple of Ānaipayanallūr and Saṅgukkal alias Vikramaśōḷanallūr. Registers that as the existing dēvadāna lands of the temple of Tirumuḍugam-Uḍaiyār were inadequate for meeting the expenses of the temple, lands in lieu thereof for feeding the Mahēśvaras in the Vikramaśōḷa-maṭha, built in the temple were, at the instance of Sōḷakōn, given free of taxes in the village Sōḷa-kūṟṟam-hiṇṭamaṅgalam in Paravūr-kūṟṟam in Iruṅgōḷap-pāḍi. These lands formed into a village named Vikramaśōḷanallūr.

cells.remarks: Unfinished. Gift of land free of taxes in Pagalavadi in Paruvur-parru consisting of thirty shares, in the name of the king, by Tirumalirolaininran alias Malavarayan, the chief of Na[d] Kuruchchi in Sevvirukkai Semba-nadu in Padi-mandalam. Out of those, 24 brahmans of the agaram Kulasekhara-chaturvedimangalam received one share each, and the Nayanmar two; two were assigned for the temple of the Nayanmar of the Tiruvirattanam-Purana-vritti. These brahmans had probably to do some service for the Vikrama-Pandyan-sand by turns of eight. Gift of taxes levied from the village of Sonniyamallar alias Rajakkayanallur and Sembaljurichchi alias Maru-konal-toduda-Pandyanallur for offerings and for the Rajakkayanayan festival instituted in the temple in the village of Paruvur. The document is signed by Dovan Pallavarayan of Adhigarigal-kallan in Muttu-kurgam in Pandimandalam.

cells.place: On the south wall of the central shrine in the Brahmapurīśvara temple at Brahmadeśam (Villupuram taluk, South Arcot district).
cells.date: 41st year, and 284 days, Ṛishabha, ba. di. Tuesday, Anusham.
cells.remarks: Incomplete. The introduction commences with the words svasti śrī. Purchase of land in Panaiyūr, the southern hamlet of this village, in the name of Brahmādhirāya-Mahādēva by the assembly of the great men at Rājarājachaturvēdimangalam, a brahmādēya and a tani-yūr in this nāḍu, a subdivision of Gaṭṭikoṇḍa-śōḷa-vaḷanāḍu. It is stated that the king consecrated in the temple of Rājarāja-Viṇṇagar-Āḷvār which was his tutelary deity along with his subordinates (maganar) Adavallan alias Kulōttunga-śōḷamuṇḍavēḷāy who was governing the place, having consecrated the god (dēva-pratishṭhai), opened sources for water (jala-pratishṭhai), destroyed the weeds and supported the wise.

cells.date: 5th year [date-calculation appendix, No. 179: Cholas—cont. Parakēsarivarman Rājēndradēva. 7th year, Mithuna, ba. di. 4, Thursday, Avittam. The day intended was apparently Thursday, 3rd June A.D. 1059, on which day nakshatra "Avittam" or "Sravistha" ended at 20 1/2 ghatikas after mean sunrise. But the tithi was ba. 5 and not ba. 4 and it ended at 27 1/2 ghatikas after mean sunrise. NOTE.—Ba. 4 probably an error for ba. 5.]
cells.remarks: The historical introduction commences with the words, "Pugal-madu etc. Registers that the devadana lands belonging to the temple of Brahmisvaramudaiya-Mahadeva and the land given for feeding tapavins in the Rajanarayan-isvaramudaiya-Nayanar temple were clubbed together as a new village called Kulottunga-Cholanallur which was declared free of taxes.

cells.remarks: Registers the grant of the village Tagarūru to Sōmayya-Gōpaya, son of Bālagōpa of Bālagōpa of Nōgūru by Sāluva-Gōvindarāja, with the consent of his younger brother the Mahāpradhāna (prime minister) Sāluva Timmarasa, under the orders of the king. The king is stated to be the son of Kathāri-Sāluva Narasimhadēva-Mahārāja, the lord of the Southern Ocean. The donee's grandfather Sōmēśvarabhaṭṭa, also called Mallikārjuna, was the guru of Vīra-Rudru, the lord of the town of Ōrun.

cells.date: Śaka 976, Jaya, Uttarāyaṇa-Saṅkrānti, Sunday. [date-calculation appendix, No. 201: Trailōkyamalladēva.]
cells.remarks: Registers that while Trailōkyamalla-Nala-Pallava-Permanaḍi was ruling the Noḷambavāḍi 32,000, Baḷḷakunde [300] and Koḍumbāḷi [300], the 120 mahājanas of Rēōhūru, granted for the worship of Jina, a garden, a wet field, 5 houses and one oil-mill, to a certain Ashṭōpavāsi-Bhaṭṭa of Dēśiga-Gaṇa. The record mentions Jagadēkamalla-Mallidēva-Chōḷamahārāja as a subordinate of the chief mentioned above. On the back of the slab is a partly damaged record of the same period, referring to a grant made to Ashṭōpavāsi-muni at Bēhūru. A certain Vīranandi-siddhānti is mentioned.

cells.place: On a slab set up in the Mallikārjunasvāmin temple in the same village (as Kallēśvarasvāmin temple). †
cells.date: Ch. Vik. 29, Tāraṇa, Vaiśākha, śu. tadige, Sunday.
cells.remarks: States that the mahājanas of the agrahāra Gaṇḍarādityana-Hoḷaḷ, having complained to the emperor (chakravartti) that Māyidēva, son of the late Hēgāḍe Būchimayya was plundering all properties of the said Hēgāḍe and his family, had the emperor sent for Boppayya, chastised him and took from him an undertaking that he and his successors should secede from the government of Hoḷaḷu. The chief did accordingly in the presence of the thirty-two thousand (representatives) of Beṇṇevūru 12, Niruṅguṇḍa 2, Baḍah-guḷi, Māṅgoḷa, Bidirahaḷḷi, Hābanūru, Honnavatti, Kuru-vaṭṭi and Mūguḷi and drank water at the temple of Tripurāntakadēva.

Gift of land for two lamps by a native of Poliyūr in Jayangoṇḍachōḷa-maṇḍalam to the same temple.

NOTE.—It is note worthy that these epigraphs, as proved by their dates, should belong to the reign of Kulōttunga-Chōla II whose dated inscription, have so far occurred only in Telugu districts (vide the article on this reign by the present writer in Epigraphia Indica, Vol. XI, page 287). There are no dates satisfying the given details in the reign of either Kulōttunga-Chōla I or Kulōttunga-Chōla III. The blank in No. 380 of 1918, which has been read conjecturally as "bahula" should be "sukla," while "pūrvapaksha" or "śu. di." in No. 528 of 1918, which is quite clear in the impression, is clearly an error for "apurapaksha" or "ba. di.," the combination of śu. 9 and nak. "Visakha" in Makara mouth not being possible except in aparapaksha. See the present writer's Eye-table.]

cells.place: On the east, north and west walls of Varadarāja-Perumāḷ temple. †
cells.remarks: Damaged and incomplete. Registers a gift of land for the temple site, for the maintenance of a flower-garden, to the god Arulāḷa-Perumāḷ-Aḷvār by a servant in the 4th year of Vikrama-Chōḷadēva, by Arumbākkilān Madurāntakan Poṇṇambalakūttan alias Porkōyil Toṇḍaimānār residing in Manavil-kōṭṭam, a district of Jayangoṇḍachōḷa-maṇḍalam, for the prosperity of the king (Perumāḷ) and the village. The gift was made at the request of the village assembly who were attending to the duties of the temple of Tribhuvanamādēvi-chaturvēdimangalam, a brahmadeya, from the month of Karkataka. The flower garden (of the image of) Parantakadēva set up in the temple of Rājarājavinnagar is referred to incidentally. Begins with the historical introduction Pūmādu-pōla, etc.

cells.remarks: Records that the bank of the tank at Tribhuvanamādēvi-chaturvēdimaṅgalam had breached and that Bhūtaṅgan-gaḷamuḍaiyāṇ Ūrriyūran Bhūpālasundaran alias Sōḷa-kōṇār had it repaired. The stone revetment was constructed by the village assembly and the Araiya-Tirumalaipaḍi-Uḍaiyāṇ alias Malaiyappaiyaṇ, a sub-hamlet of the former. The revetment was called Kuḷōttuṅgāḍu.

cells.place: On the stone slab
cells.remarks: Refers to the same transaction and registers a gift of land by Solakōn for repairing the bank and constructing the stone revetment. The paddy accruing for the repair of the tank was being mixed up with the general dues from the village and the above noted paddy were not being attended to. In lieu of this paddy was now given land in Neṭṭaippākkam alias Bhaṭṭābhiraṇḍanallūr, a hamlet of Tribhuvanamahādēvi-chaturvēdimangalam.

cells.remarks: The last of a set of plates. The boundaries of the granted village are given in Telugu. Then follows a verse in Sanskrit which states that the king gave to his preceptor Śaṅkara the village Pinapāḍu and that Śrī-nātha-Bhaṭṭāraka composed the inscription. Damaged. Registers the grant, by the king, of the village Pinapāḍu and in Chanu[rpa]lli vishaya to a Brahman called Maṇḍalāśarman of the Vatsa-gōtra who was a scholar in the (the) Vedas and the Vedāngas. The donee is stated to have been attached to (bhakta) Maṅgi Yuvarāja.

Vyāsa-Tīrtha seems to be the god of the village as a gift from Krishnaraya and the festival was called after him. Vyāsa-Tīrtha also made a gift of the serpent-vehicle to be carried in procession on the 4th day of all festivals.

cells.remarks: Gift of 100 poṇ for celebrating the day of Śrījayanti festival on which Śrī Kṛishṇa was born. In making provision for worship and offerings, it was particularly mentioned that a lamp should be kept to be represented as a child drinking milk, placing the lamp in the shrine room. The gift was engraved on stone in the name of Vaḍa Tiruvengadaiyaṛ, the kōyil-kōvi, who was the disciple of Paravastu Ayyangār at the instance of Kaṇḍāśi Rāmānujayyangār, one of the managers of the temple.

cells.date: Śaka 1446, Viśāva, Karkataka, ba. di., tritiyā, Wednesday, (Śatabhishaj).
cells.remarks: Records that the king soon after his coronation in the year Virodhi directed that the gift of villages made to the temple of Varadarāja and the Ekāmbaranātha should be of equal estimated worth and that the villagers should attend to it. But the latter gave more to Ekāmbaranātha than to Varadarāja and that, on hearing this Acyuta went to Conjeeveram in person and effected the equalization between the two temples by owning lots.

cells.place: On the north wall of the central shrine of Vikrama-Chō- ḷēśvara temple at Kanna- puram
cells.remarks: Records that in response to the request of the nagarattār of Abhimānapuram and Vikramachōḷapuram, the king ordered that the amount accruing from land taxes from the two villages should be equally divided and assigned for expenses to the two temples. Among the names of the signatories are found Ellamvalla Sōḷa Muvēndavēḷan, Vāparayadēvan, Tyāgavindadēvan, Muṇaiyadarayan, Chēdirayadēvan, Kāḍuveṭṭi, Kalappāḷarāyan and Vilāja- siṅgudēvan.

cells.place: On two pillars to the south of the Alvār-shrine behind the sanctum of Śrī-Rāma temple at Bhadrāchalam Bhadrāchalam taluk, Godāvari district.
cells.date: Śaka 1754, Nandana, Chaitra, śu. di., 9, Sunday.
cells.remarks: Registers that a certain Varada-Ramadāsu of Kaḷichi-nagara, who was an incarnation of Śrī-Rāmadāsu of the time of Tanisha, came to Bhadrāchalam and spent his time there as a devotee. He constructed the temple and performed the daily worship of the Haṣanachā-Paragu (in His Exalted Highness the Nizam's State) in the time of Nawab Nāsiruddauḷa and conferred a large part of the income of that Paragana on the temple and the Brahmins who were connected with it. Numerous other details concerning the establishment, festivals, worship, oblations, etc., of the temple are also registered.

cells.date: Śaka 1680, Kali 4882, Pramādi, Tai 21, Uttaraya-ṇa, Thursday, Pushya.
cells.remarks: Registers that Séngal Vijayaraghunatha Gopalar, son of Séngal Virayyan, son of Gopalar, who was the chief of Sirunallikkuļam in Pamba-valanādu, a division of Rajarajasola-valanadu in Rajagambhira-valanada, a district of Rajarājavalanādu, gave 46 pon of gold to the temple Jayangondanathasvāmin in Pamba-nadu for the evening service of the god thereon. Another record dated in Śaka 1680, Kali 4880, İśvara, Vaigāśi 2, is engraved in continuation of the above on the same plate and registers that 45 Rajagambhiran-pon and 9 pon of gold by the inhabitants of the sixteen divisions between the western and eastern boundaries of Pappakkudi-nadu, a sub-division of Poyyür-kõrram, a district of Jayangonda-nadu, for the midday service of the god Jayangondanatha-svamin consecrated in a temple which was newly erected after clearing some fruit-gardens.

(This supplemental record is dated in Kali 1880, Śaka 4881) (transposed). Bahu-dhanya, Vaigasi 2.

cells.remarks: Begins with the introduction "pū-maḍantai" &c. Records gift of certain tax-free lands in lieu of certain exchanges of gold belonging to the temple which were appropriated on two former occasions, viz., when Vijayarājēndra ordered, while camping in Vōṅgu-maṇḍalam, a tax of one kaḻañju of gold on every vēli of land and also when in a period of drought, the temple authorities had to improve existing irrigation. Gives also the details of a gift in the third year of Udayar Vikrama-Chōḷadēva, viz. Makara, śu. śaturdaśi, Saturday, Śatabhishaj. The village assembly met in the hall (sabhā-śālai) called Sambiyapāṇḍavi.

cells.location: Amritalur
cells.place: On a rough stone set up in a street
cells.remarks: Registers the agreement (Kaula) granted by Mahāmaṇḍalē- śvara Chinna-Timma-Rāja to the people that the settlement at the Amrita (market village) built by him to the south of Amritalur in the name of Mahāmandirāja. No taxes were payable by the settlers in the pēṭa for the first three years. After that period they were required to pay taxes on ploughs, looms, and houses, big and small. States that Nāgappa-Nāyaka the agent (karyakarta) of the King gave an agreement to the merchants, weavers, etc., of Siripuram to pay for three years, taxes on account of a plunder suffered by the people. Refers to Śrīraṅgapaṭaya who was evidently ruling then.

cells.remarks: Records that Guḍhaya, the commander (daṇḍanātha) of Mahāmaṇḍaleśvara Kuḷottuṅga Rājendra-Choḍayārāja constructed the temple of Choḍeśvara at Moparru for the merit of his father Choḍaya-Nāyaka and his mother Nāyāsāni. Gives the names of the dancing girls appointed to serve in the same temple.

cells.place: On the southern side of the eastern gateway of Choḍeśvarasvāmin temple. †
cells.remarks: Defines in a ślōka the length of the linear measures of aṅgula, vitasti and daṇḍa and states the circumference of the thumb in an aṅgula. Twelve aṅgulas make one vitasti and thirty-two vitastis make one daṇḍa. In the Telugu portion the kesaripāṭi-ghaḍa which corresponds to the daṇḍa is mentioned. A vertical line is cut over the inscription to give the exact measurement, evidently, of the vitasti. It measures a little over 1 foot and 3 inches.

cells.remarks: Damaged. Gives a descriptive praise of the (god) Gōvardhanēśa, who appeared in the form of a cowherd to his devotee Vallabha, quoting the famous verse in the Bhagavad-Gītā, which ends with "Dharmasaṁsthāpanāya sambhavāmi yuge yuge". Says also that the god became manifest (i.e., was installed) and was named Gōvardhanēśa. No date quoted. cells.remarks: Records that as a moiety of the temple lands in Kalikad-nallūr, a devadāna village, which were mortgaged to Ariyan Kariyaperumāmal, were now redeemed by Manaiyali-Paramēśvara-Nayakar, a nāyaka of Malai-mandalam for 317 panam. cells.location: Erikutti

cells.remarks: Records that Ammuṇḍu-tayyar who held the Jaghir of Erikutti ordered the construction of 2 tanks and that made a gift of 600 kuḷi of land to certain officers. The construction of the tanks was left in the hands of Nimmala Ayyappa-Nāyaka and Pērumāl-Nāyaka. Mentions also that Sattal-laṅkan (Saḍat-ulla Khan) the Nabā of Karṇāṭaka was ruling under the overlordship of Farukān Bādshā (Faruk Shiyar), the grandson of Aurangazeb.

On a rock (locally known as Perumal-rock) to the east of the village Narlampet.
On the east wall (left of entrance) of the Bairappan temple
cells.date:
Bhava, Magha, ba., 10.
Virodhi, Marga, ba., 7.
cells.remarks: Registers the grant of 100 kuntas of manya land made to the god Rambhadrasvami by Tumba Venkatava. The inscription is engraved below the figure of a horse led by a groom, preceded and followed by two attendants with swords in their hands. States that this stone was the gift of a certain Baiyapa-setti, son of Chinna-Jogi-Ganda.
